definitions.explanation: A creative work (book, film, painting, etc.) that is ordinary and lacks distinction. Not necessarily bad, but not noteworthy either.

examples.japanese: あの{映画|えいが}は{凡作|ぼんさく}だった。
{期待|きたい}していたが、{凡作|ぼんさく}に{終|お}わった。
examples.english: I had high hopes, but it turned out to be an unremarkable work.

examples.japanese: {天才|てんさい}と{呼|よ}ばれた{画家|がか}にも{凡作|ぼんさく}はある。
examples.english: Even a painter called a genius has some mediocre works.

notes:
USAGE:
{凡作|ぼんさく} is used primarily in criticism and reviews of creative works. It implies something merely average — not terrible, but lacking in originality or impact. The {凡|ぼん} character means "ordinary" or "mediocre."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {凡作|ぼんさく}に{終|お}わる (to end up as a mediocre work)
- {凡作|ぼんさく}と{言|い}わざるを{得|え}ない (one must call it mediocre)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{傑作|けっさく} (masterpiece) and {駄作|ださく} (terrible work) are at opposite ends of the quality spectrum. {凡作|ぼんさく} sits in the middle — better than {駄作|ださく} but far from {傑作|けっさく}. {佳作|かさく} (commendable work) is slightly above {凡作|ぼんさく}, indicating decent quality.
